<thought>Based on the mass spectrum (M⁺ at m/z ≈ 121 Da, with an M+1 intensity consistent with ~8 C atoms) and the ¹H NMR showing only aromatic protons (5 H, multiplet typical of a monosubstituted phenyl), the most plausible structure is acetophenone (phenyl‑methyl‑ketone). Its molecular formula C₈H₈O gives a monoisotopic mass of 120.0575 Da, so the protonated ion [M+H]⁺ appears at m/z ≈ 121.065 Da, matching the observed ion within experimental tolerance. The aromatic pattern (2 H dd + 3 H tt) aligns with a phenyl ring attached to a carbonyl, and the missing aliphatic signal likely falls outside the displayed range of the simplified NMR output. Therefore, the SMILES string for acetophenone is the best answer.</thought>
<final_answer>CC(=O)C1=CC=CC=C1</final_answer>
